assertion: The CDC's weekly influenza update for the week ending on Nov. 7, says positive tests for flu specimens were at about 11% and rising.
independent_value: CDC FluView Week 44: 5,911 of 52,287 specimens positive = 11.3%, increased vs Week 43. Warehouse search_catalog found no lab-positivity table.
measure: influenza percent positive clinical laboratories CDC weekly

assertion: More than 3% of doctors' office visits were due to flu-like symptoms.
independent_value: ILINet Week 44: 3.2% of visits for ILI (fever plus cough or sore throat), above baseline 2.9%; ILI is a symptom definition, not lab-confirmed flu, which the sentence correctly says

assertion: Louisiana tops the list as the only state in the very high category.
independent_value: CDC Week 44 ILI activity table: 1 jurisdiction Very High; Latin Times coverage names Louisiana

assertion: six states reaching new high levels ... South Carolina and Texas were the next highest, with California, Tennessee and Oregon following, also in the high category
inaccuracy: CDC counts 1 Very High + 6 High = 7 jurisdictions; the piece lists Louisiana plus five High states (six total) and omits Washington. The within-High ordering is not a CDC ranking.
independent_value: CDC Week 44: Very High 1, High 6 (up from 0 and 2); coverage lists CA, LA, OR, SC, TN, TX, WA

assertion: There are an estimated 2.6 million illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations and 2,100 deaths related to flu infections so far this season, according to the CDC.
independent_value: CDC: at least 2,600,000 illnesses, 36,000 hospitalizations, 2,100 deaths (preliminary estimates)

assertion: Five of the deaths among children have been reported to the CDC.
independent_value: CDC: five pediatric deaths this season; counted separately from the 2,100 estimate

assertion: Dr. Anna Durbin of Johns Hopkins University says the rate of flu hospitalizations in mid-October was at its highest level in the past 15 years.
speaker: Dr. Anna Durbin
inaccuracy: Durbin said highest early-season mid-October rate since 2010-11 (week ending Oct 17). Warehouse covers 2018-19 on only; pre-2018 rests on Durbin citing CDC.
warehouse_value: FluSurv-NET weekly rate week ending 2026-10-17 = 1.6/100k; 2022-23 (2022-10-15) 0.6; other seasons 0.1-0.3
sql: SELECT season,"date",estimate FROM health.cdc_resp_net_rates WHERE surveillance_network='FluSurv-NET' AND state='Overall' AND age_category='Overall' AND race='All' AND sex='All' AND data_type='Weekly Rate'
independent_value: Chief Healthcare Executive quotes Durbin: highest early season hospital rate for mid-October since 2010-2011

assertion: the flu season is starting a bit earlier
speaker: Dr. Anna Durbin
independent_value: CDC: activity is higher than typically observed at this time of year; warehouse FluSurv-NET weekly rate at Oct 17 is 1.6 vs 0.6 or less in prior seasons

assertion: I think it's really important for everyone to get a flu vaccine as soon as possible
speaker: Dr. Anna Durbin
reason: A personal recommendation (belief), not a testable fact. CDC itself recommends vaccination (FluView Week 44) but 'as soon as possible' urgency is judgment.
searched: Anna Durbin Johns Hopkins flu hospitalizations mid-October highest in 15 years

assertion: The CDC recommends an annual flu vaccine for everyone 6 months of age and older.
independent_value: CDC Week 44: vaccines recommended for persons 6 months and older

assertion: seasonal flu activity is on the rise across the country
inaccuracy: CDC: indicators rising in many parts, not uniformly (Region 9 positivity fell; Region 2 ILI fell, likely incomplete data). Warehouse FluSurv-NET weekly rate 2.7 (Nov 7) then 2.3 (Nov 14).
warehouse_value: FluSurv-NET weekly rate 2026-11-07 = 2.7, 2026-11-14 = 2.3; ARI map week 2026-11-14: 8 Moderate, none High
sql: SELECT "date",estimate FROM health.cdc_resp_net_rates WHERE surveillance_network='FluSurv-NET' AND state='Overall' AND data_type='Weekly Rate' AND season='2026-27'
